# `fine-tree` vectors (G15) — the MSB-first pin

`fine-tree.json` is the M0 **unbalanced-n golden vector** (MVP-SPEC.md
line 169; Q6 must-exist slug `fine-tree-unbalanced-n6`). Everything else it
carries is in service of one pinned property:

> **MSB-first GGM leaf indexing is the pinned property.** Leaf `i` is reached
> from `s_root` by the bits of `i` taken **most-significant first** — bit
> `d − 1`, then `d − 2`, … , then bit 0 — where `d = ⌈log₂ n⌉`
> (MVP-SPEC.md line 96). At the `n = 6` case (`d = 3`) leaf 2's path is
> therefore `(0, 1, 0)`.

That is a rule an implementation can get exactly backwards while remaining
perfectly self-consistent: an LSB-first implementation still produces one
salt per byte, still builds a tree, still verifies its own openings. It just
produces *different bytes*, and would not interoperate with anything. So the
vector pins the intermediates, not merely the outcome:

| pinned | why |
| --- | --- |
| every **used GGM node seed** (`ggm_nodes`) | an indexing change shows up at every level, not only at the root |
| every **`salt_i`** (`salts`) | this is the MSB-first pin itself: reversing the bit order changes `salt_i` for every `i` whose bit pattern is not a palindrome |
| every **RFC 6962 content-tree node** (`merkle_nodes`) | pins unbalanced promotion — the left subtree is the largest *perfect* one — level by level from the leaves up |
| **`fine_root`** | the value a manifest commits to |
| per opening: the **leaf-exact cover** and the **boundary path** | the full range proof, with the seeds and hashes a bundle would ship |

The executor additionally derives each leaf **LSB-first on purpose** and
requires the result to *differ* from the committed salt wherever the reversed
path differs. Without that, a document generated by an LSB-first
implementation would pass its own vector.

## Cases

| case | `n` | what it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unbalanced-n6` | 6 | the mandated unbalanced vector: `d = 3`, slots 6 and 7 unused, RFC 6962 promotion splits `[0,6)` into `[0,4)` + `[4,6)` |
| `n1-root-is-leaf` | 1 | `d = 0`, so `salt_0 = s_root[..16]` with **zero** derivation steps and `fine_root` is the single leaf hash |
| `n0-no-tree` | 0 | an empty file has no fine tree at all (line 78): `depth`/`fine_root` are `null` and every list is empty |
| `n5-one-past-a-power-of-two` | 5 | unused GGM slots: revealing `[4,5)` emits the single node `(1,1)`, whose slot span `[4,8)` is three-quarters unused |

## Openings

Ranges chosen so every cover shape appears:

| case | reveal | cover | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| n=6 | `{2}` | `(3,2)` | G11's first normative KAT: the deepest single-leaf node |
| n=6 | `[1,3)` | `(3,1)`, `(3,2)` | a range straddling an interior boundary — two cover nodes, three boundary hashes |
| n=6 | `[4,6)` | `(1,1)` | G11's second KAT and the **positive** case for the unused-slot allowance: the emitted node also spans slots 6 and 7, which are not real leaves |
| n=6 | `[0,6)` | `(0,0)` | full reveal — the one and only case that releases `s_root`, with an empty boundary path |
| n=5 | `[4,5)` | `(1,1)` | one real leaf, three unused slots under the same node |
| n=5 | `[0,4)` | `(1,0)` | the perfect left subtree; the ragged `[4,5)` node is the boundary |
| n=5 | `[0,5)` | `(0,0)` | full reveal |
| n=1 | `[0,1)` | `(0,0)` | full reveal of a one-byte file |

`releases_s_root` is `true` **iff** the range is `[0, n)` — a consequence of
leaf-exactness, not a separate rule (MVP-SPEC.md line 96). The vector asserts
that equivalence on every opening.

## Node addressing

Both `cover` and `boundary` nodes carry `(level, index)` — decision D9's
canonical form, `level` counted from the root, `index` a position within the
level whose `level` bits *are* the MSB-first path. Content-tree
(boundary-path) nodes can span a truncated interval at a ragged right edge,
so their address is the **deepest** grid slot whose real span equals the
node's leaf interval (`docs/format/registry-v1.md` §5). At `n = 6` the node
over `[4,6)` is `(2,2)`, not `(1,1)`.

## Provenance and regeneration

All fixture material is **NON-SECRET** (project rule 6): the master secret is
the documented fixed test seed `00 01 … 1f` (`testdata/README.md`), and the
synthetic file seed is the project's `alternate_test_secret` construction

```text
s_root = SHA-256("antseal G15 fine-tree s_root" || W)
```

so it is a genuinely distinct seed that is still a deterministic function of
the documented one. Never real vault material.

`gen_vectors.py` is an **independent** implementation of the whole stack
(Python standard library only, written from MVP-SPEC.md, sharing no code with
antseal-core). It carries its own self-test — the spec's worked statements
(`path_bits(2, 3) == [0,1,0]`, `salt_0 = s_root[..16]` at `d = 0`, both G11
cover KATs, and exhaustive leaf-exactness over every range of every case's
`n`) — and refuses to emit without it passing. Run it to *verify*, never to
silently regenerate:

```sh
python3 gen_vectors.py | diff - fine-tree.json
```

The Rust side regenerates the same document from antseal-core's public API in
`crates/antseal-core/tests/fine_tree_vectors.rs` and diffs it field by field,
so a construction or indexing change fails CI with the offending field named.
A byte change to `fine-tree.json` is a **format event** (`../../README.md`):
regenerate, re-run `scripts/vector-freeze.sh --update`, and justify the digest
diff in the commit.
